newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis kill Palestinian, arrest militant Jew.
newsitem.headline: Israelis kill Palestinian, arrest militant Jew.

text.p: Israeli troops shot dead a Palestinian man and wounded 11 people on Sunday in the bloodiest West Bank violence since Arabs and Jews pulled back from the brink of war in September.

In Hebron, Jewish militant leader Noam Federman was detained without trial in the first of several arrests Israel said would be needed for the peaceful handover of that troubled West Bank city to Palestinian rule.
Thousands of Palestinians from the West Bank and Gaza Strip returned to jobs in Israel with the easing of a closure tightened last month because of Israeli security concerns.
Violence erupted when soldiers stopped 200 Palestinians from four villages on their way to a protest against confiscation of 1,250 acres (500 acres) for Jewish settlement, witnesses said.
"This is another serious breaching from the settlers against our people," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in Gaza.
The unrest, in Deir Kidis village near Ramallah, was the bloodiest since an outburst six weeks ago claimed the lives of 60 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers.
"The soldiers called on the people to return and blocked their way, but demonstrators refused, so the army shot at demonstrators' legs and chests," one witness said.
Atallah Amireh, 36, was killed and 11 people were wounded, medical officials said. The Israeli army was investigating.
Israel still occupies much of the West Bank despite having handed parts to Palestinian rule under peace deals with the PLO.
Federman, a former leader of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement, was taken from his home in Hebron at 5 a.m.
His wife Elisheva said police came with an order to hold him without trial for two months and searched their house.
She said police took a bumper sticker calling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat a dangerous twosome.

Concerns for the security of the Jews have held up the handover of the flashpoint city holy to Moslems and Jews as the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham. Some 400 Jews live and study there in the heart of 100,000 Arabs.

"Arrests are being made because for the moment all must be done so that the handover from one side to the other side in Hebron will be a quiet handover," Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said.
On Saturday he said Israel would detain dozens of Jewish militants who might actively oppose the handover. Kach and its offshoots favour expelling Arabs from areas under Israeli rule.

Israel and the PLO appear to be on the verge of closing a deal to hand over the city to Palestinian rule. But chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the two peace teams had not met since last Wednesday.

Netanyahu dismissed an Israeli media report that some army officers favoured evacuating the Jews from Hebron. The Israeli leader told reporters: "In the name of this government? Forget it. It will never happen."
A report that women living in the city planned to set themselves afire in protest on the day of the pullout was denied by several of them in interviews with Israeli radio stations.

Descendants of Jews who lived in Hebron before a massacre by Arabs in 1929 met Palestinian legislators at city hall to say they, who presently live in Israel, rather than the settlers, represented the old Jewish community of Hebron.
"The settlers today don't represent the old community of Hebron. We have no connection with them," Moshe Galmor told Israel Radio.

Palestinian Mayor Mustafa Natshe, greeted the visitors warmly, saying: "There are many Jewish extremists in the city of Hebron today. We the people of Hebron are ready to receive the Jews who lived here, to return and live in peace with us as was the case 400 years ago during the Ottomans' rule."
